newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady, RBI mops up forward dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady, RBI mops up forward dlrs.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Thursday at 35.8850/8950 per dollar in tight range-bound trade, little changed from the opening 35.8950/9050, dealers said.
They said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) bought spot dollars at 35.900/925 level earlier on Thursday.
Fresh dollar sales at the higher level and heavy dollar inflows from the Delhi market later in the day helped the rupee recover mildly, dealers said.
The RBI's last purchase purchase price was 35.8900 per dollar, they said.
"I don't think they bought large quantities," said a dealer.
The rupee saw a low of 35.915 on Thursday, dealers said.
The RBI bought dollars across wide maturities in the forward market on Thursday, pushing up premia, dealers said.
The six month annualised forward premium closed Thursday at 6.97 percent, up from the previous close of 6.80 percent.
"I think the RBI is helping exporters to cover their forward dollars until the year-end," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
"After March 31, I doubt if RBI will buy forwards," he said.
